dialogue.content: こんにちは。本日はよろしくお願いいたします。定刻より始めさせていただきます。
dialogue.English: Hello. Thank you for meeting with me today. We’ll begin as scheduled.

dialogue.content: マッチングの承認が遅くなってしまい申し訳ありませんでした。どうぞよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: I apologize for the delay in confirming our session. I'm looking forward to speaking with you.

dialogue.content: いえいえ！お気遣いありがとうございます！よろしくお願いいたします
dialogue.English: Not at all! Thank you for your thoughtfulness. I look forward to working with you.

dialogue.content: こんにちは。相談員です。本日はよろしくお願いいたします。はじめに年齢、性別、相談内容を教えていただけますか？
dialogue.English: Hello. I'm your counselor. Thank you for being here today. To start, could you please tell me your age, gender, and what you'd like to discuss?

dialogue.content: 34歳女性職場の人間関係で悩んでいます
dialogue.English: I'm a 34-year-old woman, and I'm struggling with relationships at work.

dialogue.content: 実は9月から新しい部署に異動になりました。その上司の対応がきつくて、気持ちが参っています。
dialogue.English: Actually, I was transferred to a new department in September. My supervisor's attitude is harsh, and it’s wearing me down.

dialogue.content: ご相談ありがとうございます。そうなのですね。それはしんどいですよね。
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing that. I see. That sounds really tough.

dialogue.content: 上司の方はどのようにきついのですか？
dialogue.English: In what ways is your supervisor harsh?

dialogue.content: はい。言葉がそっけない言い方がキツい優しさとか思いやりとかが感じられません
dialogue.English: Yes. Their words are curt and their tone is harsh. I don't feel any kindness or consideration from them.

dialogue.content: それは辛くなりますよね。一緒に仕事したくなくなりますよね。
dialogue.English: That must be upsetting. It probably makes you not want to work with them.

dialogue.content: 実際に相談者さんが言われたことはどんなことなのですか？
dialogue.English: What kinds of things have they actually said to you?

dialogue.content: そうですね。今日で約1週間ですが、どんどん辛くなります。
dialogue.English: Well... it's been about a week now, and it's getting harder and harder.

dialogue.content: 新しい部署でまだ勝手がわからないので「これはどうしたらいいですか」と聞いたら、「どうしたらいいか自分で考えて！」と突き放された感じでした
dialogue.English: Since I’m still unfamiliar with the new department, when I asked, 'What should I do with this?' they snapped, 'Figure it out yourself!' It felt very dismissive.

dialogue.content: １週間しかいないのにそんなに辛くあたってくる人いるのですね。それは悲しい辛くなりますよね。
dialogue.English: To be treated so harshly when you've only been there for a week... That must be very disheartening and painful for you.

dialogue.content: 上司の人は一日中そのような接しかたなのですか？
dialogue.English: Is your supervisor like that with you throughout the day?

dialogue.content: 確かに、元いた部署でもやっていた作業ではあったのですが、やり方が違ったらいけないと思って聞いただけなのに…
dialogue.English: It's true that it was a task I used to do in my old department, but I was just asking because I was worried the method might be different...

dialogue.content: そうですよね。新しいから確認しますよね。
dialogue.English: That makes sense. It’s natural to check when things are new.

dialogue.content: はい忙しいからかも知れないです。私と同時に新しく入社した20代の男の子が同じ部署に配属されたので
dialogue.English: Yes, maybe it’s because they’re busy. A young man in his twenties who joined the company at the same time as me was assigned to the same department,

dialogue.content: そっちにかかりきり
dialogue.English: and they're completely tied up with him.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。でも忙しからと言って辛くあたるのは違いますよね。
dialogue.English: I see. But being busy is no excuse to treat you harshly, is it?

dialogue.content: そうだと思います
dialogue.English: I agree.

dialogue.content: その20代の男の子に対してもその上司は辛くあたっているのですか？
dialogue.English: Is the supervisor harsh with that young man in his 20s as well?

dialogue.content: それが、全くの新人さんなので丁寧に教えているように感じます。私は1月に入社しているので基本的な事はわかっていると思っていると思います
dialogue.English: Actually, it seems they are teaching him patiently because he's brand new to the company. Since I joined in January, I think they assume I already know the basics.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。でも基本的なことがわかっているかどうかのコンセンサスは上司から聞いてきてほしいですよね。
dialogue.English: I see. But it would be better if your supervisor confirmed with you what you know instead of just assuming, wouldn't it?

dialogue.content: 相談者さんからすると今の部署は肩身が狭いというか、いずらい感じでしょうか？
dialogue.English: So for you, does it feel like you're walking on eggshells in your current department, or that it's an uncomfortable place to be?

dialogue.content: そうですよね。同じフロアにいたとはいえ、部署が変わればやり方も違うのに…
dialogue.English: Exactly. Even though I was on the same floor, when you change departments, the way things are done is different...

dialogue.content: 確かに居心地は悪いです
dialogue.English: It's definitely uncomfortable.

dialogue.content: でもまだ慣れていないからかもとも思います
dialogue.English: But I also think it might just be because I'm not used to it yet.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。その上司にきつくあたられた時は相談者さんはどのように対応されるのですか？
dialogue.English: I see. When your supervisor is harsh with you, how do you respond?

dialogue.content: とにかくできる限りのことをしようとしています。嫌な気持ちになりますが、頑張ろうと思ってます
dialogue.English: I just try to do everything I possibly can. It feels awful, but I'm trying to persevere.

dialogue.content: なるほど。嫌な気持ちになりますよね。でもそのような状況でも頑張られているのは凄いと思います。
dialogue.English: I see. It must feel awful. But I think it's amazing that you're trying so hard even in that situation.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます機嫌を損ねないように必死です
dialogue.English: Thank you. I'm desperate not to upset them.

dialogue.content: その必死さはすごくわかります。とても大変ですよね。その上司の方をまわりの人はどう思っているのですか？
dialogue.English: I can really understand that desperation. It must be very tough. What do the people around you think of that supervisor?

dialogue.content: キツいところがあると思っている人もいるみたいです。今日初めて同じ部署の先輩と話すことができました
dialogue.English: It seems some people do think they can be harsh. I was able to talk to a senior colleague in the same department for the first time today.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。先輩とお話しできたのですね。その先輩はどのように話していましたか？
dialogue.English: I see, so you were able to speak with a senior colleague. What did they have to say?

dialogue.content: その上司は忙しくなってくるとやはり口調がキツくなるようです。でも、私はきらわれているのかなと感じてしまうくらい厳しいな
dialogue.English: It seems that when that supervisor gets busy, their tone does become harsh. But with me, it’s so severe that I end up feeling like they might dislike me.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。その先輩も相談者さんがキツく言われているのを見て、いつも以上にキツく言っていると感じているのですかね？
dialogue.English: I see. So your senior colleague saw how you were being spoken to and felt that the supervisor was being harsher than usual?

dialogue.content: はい。あの言い方はキツイよねと言ってくれました
dialogue.English: Yes. They told me, 'That way of speaking is harsh, isn’t it?'

dialogue.content: 先輩が思うぐらいキツい言い方はそうとうキツいのですね。相談者さんはよく耐えておられるなとびっくりしております。
dialogue.English: If even a senior colleague thinks it's harsh, then it must be quite severe. I'm amazed that you're enduring it so well.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございますせっかく入社した会社なので辞めたくないなと思ってます
dialogue.English: Thank you. I don't want to quit, especially since I worked so hard to get into this company.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。まだまだこれからですよね。
dialogue.English: I understand. And your time there has really just begun.

dialogue.content: 相談者さんの中で今後はどうなっていけたらいいと思っていらっしゃいますか？
dialogue.English: What are your hopes for how things will go from here?

dialogue.content: 早く仕事に慣れて、上司の顔色を伺わなくても自分の裁量でできるようになれたらいいです
dialogue.English: I'd like to get used to the work quickly so I can do things on my own without having to worry about my supervisor's mood.

dialogue.content: なるほど。すごく前向きなお考えで、素晴らしいです。
dialogue.English: I see. That’s a very positive outlook—it's wonderful.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございますでも仕事に慣れる前に、メンタルが参ってしまいそうで…どうにかしないととは思います
dialogue.English: Thank you. But I'm worried my mental health will give out before I can get used to the work... I feel like I have to do something.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。心配になりますよね。
dialogue.English: That's understandable. It's definitely a concern.

dialogue.content: はい。あの上司を思い浮かべると辛さが出てきてしまいます
dialogue.English: Yes. When I picture that supervisor, the pain just wells up.

dialogue.content: 辛いですよね。わかります。では、ご相談はメンタルが参らないようにどうするか？もしくは早く仕事に慣れるためにどうするか？このお二つが悩みかと思いましたが、いかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: That is painful, I understand. So, would you say your concerns are, one, how to keep your mental health from suffering, and two, how to get used to the work more quickly? Does that sound right?

dialogue.content: そうですね。
dialogue.English: Yes, that’s right.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。時間的にどちらか一つしか扱えないかもしれませんが、優先順位をつけるとしたらどちらでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Thank you. We may only have time to address one of those today. If you had to prioritize, which would it be?

dialogue.content: メンタルが優先かなと
dialogue.English: I think my mental health is the priority.

dialogue.content: 承知いたしました。ではメンタル面でお話をさせていただければと思います。
dialogue.English: Understood. Then let's focus our discussion on the mental health aspect.

dialogue.content: はいお願いします
dialogue.English: Yes, please.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。もう少しお話を聞かせていただきたいと思うのですが、上司が相談者さん以外の人にキツく言っているところは見たことありますか？もしくは見ていないところでも今は誰にでもキツくあたるという状況なのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Thank you. I’d like to ask a bit more: Have you seen your supervisor speak harshly to anyone other than you? Or, even if you haven’t seen it, does it seem like they’re being harsh to everyone right now?

dialogue.content: 今は私に対してだけキツい感じがします。そもそも好き嫌いが激しそうなので、全く話さない人もいるようです
dialogue.English: Right now, it feels like they're only harsh with me. It seems they have strong likes and dislikes, and there are some people they don't talk to at all.

dialogue.content: なるほど。ではその上司は部署では嫌われ者的な立ち位置なのですかね？
dialogue.English: I see. So is that supervisor something of a disliked figure within the department?

dialogue.content: うーん感情的な面があるので、みんな機嫌を気にしています。嫌いというより、扱いが難しい
dialogue.English: Hmm... they have an emotional side, so everyone is mindful of their mood. It's less that they're disliked and more that they're difficult to handle.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。めんどくさいタイプなのですね。
dialogue.English: I see. They sound like a bit of a handful.

dialogue.content: そうですね。めんどくさいですね
dialogue.English: Yes, they’re a handful.

dialogue.content: 先輩と初めてお話しできたと仰っていましたが、話できてお気持ちはどうでしたか
dialogue.English: You mentioned you were able to speak with a senior colleague for the first time. How did you feel after talking with them?

dialogue.content: 気持ちをわかってくれる人がいてとても嬉しかったです救われました
dialogue.English: I was so happy that there was someone who understood how I felt. It was such a relief.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。それはよかったです。メンタル面で辛いお気持ちを緩和する方法の一つは、やはりその辛いお気持ちを溜めずにアウトプットすることです。
dialogue.English: I see. That's wonderful. One way to alleviate mental strain is to not bottle up those difficult feelings, but to express them.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね
dialogue.English: Oh, is that so?

dialogue.content: あとやはり同じ職場に気持ちをわかってくれる人がいるというだけで、かなり助けられるものなので、どんどん他の先輩などとお話しした方がよいと思います。
dialogue.English: Also, just having someone at work who understands how you feel can be a huge help, so I think it would be good to talk more with other senior colleagues.

dialogue.content: そうですね。少しずついろいろな人に話しかけてみようかと思います
dialogue.English: You're right. I think I'll try talking to different people, little by little.

dialogue.content: いいと思います。せっかく入った会社なので、こんなことで終わってしまうのは勿体無いと思います。
dialogue.English: I think that's a good idea. You worked hard to get into this company, so it would be a shame for it to end over something like this.

dialogue.content: はい。そうですよね。
dialogue.English: Yes, you're right.

dialogue.content: お一人で気持ちをかかえる必要はないので、どんどん仲間を作ってください。お時間になってしまいました。ここまでお話しされていかがだったでしょうか？
dialogue.English: You don't have to carry these feelings all by yourself, so please continue to build allies. It looks like our time is up. How do you feel after talking about this today?

dialogue.content: はい、少しでも話せる人を作ろうと思えました
dialogue.English: Yes, I feel encouraged to find people I can talk with, even if it's just a few.

dialogue.content: よかったです。まだまだお話足りない部分あったかと思います。またお気軽にご相談きてください。
dialogue.English: I'm glad to hear that. I'm sure there's more we could have discussed. Please feel free to schedule another session anytime.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございますまた相談させていただきます
dialogue.English: Thank you. I'll be in touch for another session.

dialogue.content: 是非、またお話聞かせてください。今後の相談者さんの活躍を応援させていただきます。それではこれで本日の相談を終わらせていただきます。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Please do. I'd be happy to listen again. I'll be rooting for your success. With that, we'll conclude today's session. Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: 本日はありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Thank you for your time today.

dialogue.content: 時間過ぎてしまってすみません。お疲れ様でした。
dialogue.English: I'm sorry for going over time. Take care.
